1.why: All six screens are static, flat cards with no carousels, animations, or pop-up dialogs; only a static Logs panel and a fixed 'Stay safe' notice are present.

2.why: Each screen has one large bold heading and a single dark-blue primary button, though the persistent yellow 'Stay safe' box and dark Logs panel compete visually with the actual task card.

3.why: Each step shows only one short form with a clearly labelled field and one obvious action button, so the needed control is easy to locate, but the step indicator (1. Request / 2. Token / 3. Verify) never highlights the current step, which weakens orientation.

4.why: The flow is broken into small steps with on-screen instructions, but the user must carry a long recovery token (l1pidUnQZsyQrIME8Dbej...) and a 6-digit code across screens and remember/re-enter the new password twice.

5.why: No password manager hint, autofill affordance, 'remember me' checkbox, show-password toggle, or paste helper appears on any screen, including the login/reset password screens.

6.why: Nothing saved or previously familiar is surfaced — no masked email/phone recall, no pre-filled token, no account name shown; the token only appears in a raw developer Logs panel.

7.why: Instructional text is one to two short sentences in plain language with good contrast and clear headings (e.g. 'Use 12 or more characters with upper- and lower-case letters, a number, and a symbol').

8.why: No error state is visible in any of the six screenshots — no inline validation, no error text explaining a problem or how to correct it.

9.why: The password rule is described in words but no concrete example password, email format example, or token/code format example (e.g. '6 digits, like 123456') is shown next to any input field.

10.why: Only one authentication path is offered (token + code + password); there is no visible choice between password, code, or face/biometric login, so the statement about clear choices among such options does not hold.

11.why: Every screen presents at most one or two inputs and one primary action, with only a single secondary option ('Enter it manually') on step 1, so the user is never overloaded with choices.

12.why: The final screen clearly confirms 'Recovery complete... password has been updated and the privacy conditions have been accepted', but intermediate steps give no visible success confirmation other than advancing, with feedback buried in the technical Logs panel.

13.why: Each step has a brief explanatory sentence, but there are no tips, tooltips, help links, or 'What is a recovery token?' guidance for unfamiliar concepts like tokens and MFA codes.

14.why: Only the final screen offers 'Return to recovery start'; no back link, 'resend code', or 'edit email' option is visible on any intermediate step, so recovering from a mistake mid-flow is not supported.

15.why: All six screens reuse an identical layout: same header, same three-step indicator, one white card with heading/label/field/blue button, same yellow 'Stay safe' box and Logs panel in the same positions.
